Total on-balance-sheet commercial deposits were basically flat over the last six month-ends: **$23.61B on Apr-30 and $23.58B on Sep-30, down $34M (-0.1%)**. Middle Market is the only segment growing, and fast enough to offset small or moderate declines in every other segment.

**On-balance-sheet deposit balances by segment, month-end ($M)**

| Segment | Apr-30 | May-31 | Jun-30 | Jul-31 | Aug-31 | Sep-30 | Change Apr–Sep | % | Share Sep |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Large Corporate (LC) | 16,949.6 | 16,938.5 | 16,753.2 | 16,773.5 | 16,721.1 | 16,710.5 | -239.2 | -1.4% | 70.9% |
| Middle Market (MM) | 3,471.6 | 3,536.5 | 3,590.7 | 3,654.4 | 3,710.1 | 3,758.4 | **+286.8** | **+8.3%** | 15.9% |
| Public Sector & NFP (PUB) | 2,387.9 | 2,388.0 | 2,383.7 | 2,360.9 | 2,360.7 | 2,358.1 | -29.9 | -1.3% | 10.0% |
| Commercial Real Estate (CRE) | 585.4 | 576.9 | 567.5 | 556.6 | 545.8 | 536.6 | **-48.8** | **-8.3%** | 2.3% |
| Business Banking (BB) | 218.2 | 217.2 | 216.7 | 216.7 | 215.8 | 215.0 | -3.2 | -1.5% | 0.9% |
| **Total** | **23,612.9** | **23,657.1** | **23,511.8** | **23,562.1** | **23,553.6** | **23,578.7** | **-34.2** | **-0.1%** | 100% |

**Which segments are growing or shrinking**
- **Growing: Middle Market.** It rose every month, by roughly $50–65M a month, for +8.3% overall. Its account count actually fell from 812 to 801, so the growth comes from higher balances in existing accounts, not new accounts.
- **Shrinking steadily: Commercial Real Estate.** It fell every month, by about $9–11M a month, for -8.3%. This is the steepest decline in percentage terms, though the segment is small.
- **Drifting down slightly:**
  - **Large Corporate (-1.4%):** Most of the $239M decline came in June (-$185M). The other months were flat to slightly down. Because LC is 71% of the book, it is the largest decline in dollars.
  - **Public Sector & NFP (-1.3%):** Most of the decline came in July (-$23M).
  - **Business Banking (-1.5%):** A slow, steady decline, with account count down from 714 to 704.
- **Net effect:** Middle Market's $287M gain almost exactly offsets the $321M combined decline in the other four segments.

**Sources and definitions**
- **Main source:** BANK_DEMO.MART.DEP_BAL_SEG_MTH (month-end on-balance-sheet deposit balances by segment). Segment names come from REF.SEGMENT.
- **Check against account-level data:** I rebuilt the figures from DEPOSITS.DEP_BAL_MTHLY, DEP_ACCT and CORE.CLIENT. Every segment and month matches the mart exactly, with no duplicate rows and no accounts missing a segment.
- **What counts as a deposit:** Checking (DDA), money market (MMDA) and CDs, the products REF.PRODUCT marks as on-balance-sheet. I left out the off-balance-sheet investment sweep (SWP). It holds about $7.9B for LC and $1.8B for MM, and none in the other segments. Including it would overstate deposits.
- **Old version of the mart not used:** I didn't use MART.DEP_BAL_SEG_MTH_OLD. It includes the sweep balances and has no CRE segment; CRE balances appear to be counted under MM. Its figures will not match the table above.
- **Assumptions:**
  - "Last six month-ends" means Apr-30 through Sep-30, 2026.
  - Each client is assigned to their current segment in CORE.CLIENT. No segment history is available.
  - "Growing" or "shrinking" is judged on the Apr-to-Sep change and how consistent the month-to-month direction is.
